$comment: Machine-readable contracts for Wyrd's Evidence Thread components. `components` lists exactly what is built (every export of packages/ui/src/lib/index.ts plus the host chrome) and approved-but-unbuilt chrome (`status: "spec"`). `catalog: true` marks a component a view document may place by name and must equal packages/ui/src/lib/catalog.json; `catalog: false` marks components only trusted code composes, including chrome that resolves tenant identity, session state and navigation, which an authored view must never place, replace or impersonate. `consumers` lists where a component is used. `styles` holds shared visual rules that are not components of their own, with the components that implement them. The rendered reference is ./renders/styleguide.html; gen-theme.test.mjs pins the catalog and export sets.

altitudes.quiet: workbench default — 1px --border rule, 2px radius, no elevation
altitudes.raised: the page's single attention surface — 1px --text rule, no elevation
altitudes.flat: subordinate block — 1px --border-soft rule, no fill change

ownership.$comment: Evidence Thread semantics. See DESIGN.md 'Never colour alone': status pairs such as --ok and --danger can collapse under colour-vision deficiency, so no meaning in this system may rest on hue alone.
ownership.rule: Indigo (--declare) is Declaration, links, selection, focus, and the primary action. Green (--observe) is observed fact. Lime (--evidence) is reserved for retained Evidence, the Wyrd mark spine, and evidence-capture feedback — never a secondary action, hover, or wash. Lime is a fill carrying --evidence-ink, never text on a light surface.
ownership.redundancy: Status carries a glyph, thresholds carry a tick, chart series carry a dash and a marker. Colour is never the sole carrier of a meaning.

props.headline?: { value: string; detail?: string; tone?: string }

rules: One chart over read-only SQL: timeseries, bar, stat or table.
A non-populated state renders EmptyState in place of the plot and never a value; a degraded terminal draws the plot with its partial notice.
The footer names the exact SQL and offers Open in Query with the executed binds.
A timeseries lists its series with their latest, largest and mean plotted values; unticking a series hides its line, and the series keeps its style while hidden.

A host may key the series by typed `identity` columns instead: every recorded point stays on its own series, nothing is summed or folded, and the series table shows the exact `summary` rows under the same identity.
Past twenty series only the first twenty start shown, and the table says so.
A host that passes `shown` owns which series are drawn and hears each change through `onseries`.
A `headline` sets its value beside the title with a muted detail, and a `note` reads under the plot.

`compact` draws a headline overview tile without the table and footer: a 56px plot with no axis text, its time labels beneath, and a key when the host names several `colors`; `bars` stacks a timeseries' series as bars, coloured by `colors` when the host names a colour per caption.
Series take the palette's series order by position unless the host names a colour, and every fill is drawn at full strength.

A host `heading` replaces the chart's own header and splits it into two cards: the plot under that heading, then the selectable series summary with Show all and Open in Query in place of the SQL footer.
A keyed series' caption stays one line; opening it lists every recorded identity cell, and an equal-instant sample keeps its own marker and tooltip value.
A keyed result's `text` column, when present, is the tooltip's spelling of each value, so a host-qualified value such as a lower bound reads `≥`.
One exact Card version: name, kind, version select, lifecycle status, copyable identity, host tabs and Open in Observe.
The version listing has its own state, so a failed listing never hides the Card itself.
Every registered Card version, one row each in registration order, with the filters cards.list takes.
Filters and paging are host actions, so the host owns the applied state (its URL) and a reload or Back restores it.
A whole row opens its exact version.
An exact Card's server-managed facts, or, with `yaml`, the whole Card as the server returned it.
Nothing here is editable.
An exact Card's server-derived relationships: the Cards it references, then the Cards that reference it, each an exact version the host can open.
The files registration recorded for one exact Card version, as stored: relative path, size, SHA-256 digest and content type.

An exact Prompt as authored, which is exactly what the provider receives: provider, model and response format, then portable system text and numbered turns, or the native format's body unchanged, extension fields included.
The variables the server's Prompt compiler derived from an exact Prompt.
The Agents whose spec references an exact Prompt, each with its execution route and the Services that reference it.
A refused Agent read keeps its row.
The authored differences between two registered versions of one Prompt, from the other version to the selected one.
Choosing the other version is a host action.
An exact Verifier as declared: its description, its graph, and the authored declaration of the selected node.
Definition only: no execution state, and nothing edits the Verifier.
States: populated, denied, error, loading.
The Services and Agents whose bindings pin an exact Verifier version, each binding's subject and when it runs.
A refused owner read keeps its row.
States: populated, empty, denied, error, loading. An owner opens through card.open; without a host handler the row is not a control.

props.selected?: string, bindable: the selected node key

rules: A read-only Svelte Flow drawing of declared inputs, steps, attached and whole-Verifier requirements under stage headings, with labelled dependency arrows.
Nothing drags, connects or deletes; no execution colour or state is drawn.
Laid out once from topology: selection, focus and zoom never move a node.
Selection and focus use --declare; arrow keys move between nodes.
One ruled panel: an uppercase title, an optional muted note saying where its facts come from, optional head controls, then the body.
Tables, code blocks and row buttons inside a panel share these rules.
A row of totals over the range, each with its per-bucket trend.
A stat with nothing recorded reads "—", never 0; cost shows one amount per recorded currency and never adds currencies together.
Value counts of each facet column under the list's own WHERE and range.
Choosing a value asks the host to filter by it; a null value reads "not set" and filters by IS NULL.
Values already in the WHERE render pressed.
A facet shows its first values and expands to every value read; when the read found more than it returns, the count of hidden values says so with "+".
A severity text value reads in the colour of the highest severity number recorded with it.
Signal rows as typed cells: one row per root span for traces, one per span, log record or metric point otherwise, or the rows of authored SQL.
Trace rows carry span and error counts read for the visible traces only.
Only a signal list reads canonical columns: its headings are words and its durations, statuses, instants and services are typed cells.
Authored SQL keeps its returned headings and values as text, whatever its aliases are called.

A live list holds what is on screen, rows and counts together, while the reader hovers, focuses or scrolls it, after it opens a record until the reader resumes, or while the host pauses it; it offers "↑ N new" instead of moving rows under the pointer.
The footer states the returned extent and never a total it did not read.
A trace, span or log list sorts on the server: a sortable heading asks the host to read it again in that column's order, and Newer and Older ask for the page before the first row or after the last.
Authored SQL is refused rather than truncated, so its rows are complete and sort in the page.
Columns hides read columns; a host that passes `oncolumns` instead offers every column the signal may show and reads the reader's choice again.
CSV saves the rows and columns on screen.
A host that passes `controls` places Wrap, Columns and CSV in that element, such as its list bar, instead of above the table; a host `tools` snippet renders before them.

Span rows show their shortened trace and parent span ids before Duration, and trace rows their counts before Status; a log record's severity reads in its level's colour, decided by the recorded severity number.
Every retained span of one trace as a tree against the trace's timeline.
Levels below the second start collapsed, except the path to the selected span; a collapsed span shows how many children it holds.
"Expand all" opens every level and "Errors only" keeps error spans and their ancestors.
An axis marks round offsets from the trace start up to its end.

Names come from data and never colour a span: each recorded service takes the series palette's colour by first appearance, named in the Services key, and an error span takes the failure colour beside its ✕ by recorded status alone.
One stored span or log record, whole.
A span reads as GenAI messages beside its other attributes, with Attributes, Events, Exception and Raw tabs counted from what was recorded; a log record reads as its body and attributes.
A recorded exception heads either.
Message roles and parts come from the recorded message attributes; a value that is not the GenAI message shape shows as recorded.
A section with nothing recorded names the attribute or column that would fill it; nothing is inferred.
The one place a component says there is nothing to draw and why.
The state word is always written beside its glyph; `code` is the server's stable Wyrd error code verbatim.
One typed action control.
The host reports each action's state: `pending` disables the control so an intent is never sent twice, and a refusal or failure stays visible beside it until the next attempt.
One exact Card reference, `Kind/name@version`; a link only when the host supplies one.
A verification verdict as a StatusPill: the word and glyph carry the result.
A status badge.
Tone drives border, label and tint; every non-neutral tone carries a glyph so status never rests on hue alone.
A neutral trend polyline beside a labeled value; shape carries the trend, never status.
One duration against the longest in its set: the bar is positional, the text carries the value.
A side panel on the native modal <dialog>: focus trapping, Escape and the backdrop come from the platform, and a click on the backdrop closes it like Escape.
The host owns `open`; closing reports through `onclose`.
A host may widen it with `width` (never past the viewport), replace the title text with a `heading` (the title stays its accessible name) and add header `tools` before Close.
a persistent left rail beside the page; the rail collapses to icons, and below 768px it becomes a top bar
1px --border rule between rail and page on a neutral --bg canvas
trusted application chrome, not catalog: it frames every authored view and must never be placeable by one

props.groups: Array<Array<{ label: string, href?: string, icon: string }>>

rules: groups: Home and Cards, then Observe, Verify, and Query, separated by a 1px rule; Settings and the identity menu sit in the foot
a destination without href is not delivered yet: it stays visible, aria-disabled, and says so in its title; deferred work is not listed at all
active item takes a --declare-soft wash and a 2px --declare inset marker, positional as well as tinted
brand slot is the generated Wyrd mark followed by the Wyrd wordmark in --font-sans
the identity menu holds tenant switch, Account, theme, and Sign out as .app-control buttons
trusted application chrome, not catalog: it owns navigation, which an authored view must never redirect
min-height 48px, 10px 16px padding, 1px --border bottom rule
breadcrumb in --font-mono; the last crumb is aria-current=page and every earlier crumb is a link
the theme control is a small button (30px, 12px) naming the mode it switches to
trusted application chrome, not catalog
the root layout sets data-mode from src/lib/theme.svelte.ts; the wyrd-mode cookie persists the choice so SSR paints the right mode on first byte
every token resolves beneath data-mode; light and dark change values, never structure
trusted application chrome, not catalog: it is composed by the layout, never placed by name
WYRD in --font-mono, 10px, --weight-strong, on a --declare fill with --declare-ink text; 4px 12px padding, 2px --border rule, 2px radius
sits immediately after the Wyrd wordmark on the sign-in and tenant-entry surfaces
names the product the surface belongs to; it is identity, never a control
trusted application chrome, not catalog: an authored view must never label itself as a product
primary = --declare fill and border with --declare-ink label, the one strong action on a surface
default = --surface fill with --text label; lime is reserved for retained Evidence and never marks an action
1px --border rule, 2px radius, 32px tall, 13px --font-sans; the compact form is 30px and 12px
hover moves to --surface-hover; disabled drops to 0.6 opacity with a not-allowed cursor
no lift, sink, or offset motion: state is carried by fill and rule
focus-visible draws a 2px --declare outline with offset so it stays visible on every fill
tone is a status signal, not decoration
tone drives border, label, and tint from one --bc custom property; --ok/--warn/--danger each clear 4.5:1 as text on --surface and --bg in both modes
1px border in tone colour, 12% tinted fill, 2px radius

MUST render an aria-hidden glyph before the label — ok=✓ warn=! danger=✕ running=●. Status hues can collapse under colour-vision deficiency, so a colour-only badge makes pass and fail identical for some readers.
neutral takes no glyph and no tint: 'neutral' means no status, and a 12% --muted wash lands at 4.46:1 in dark, which the contrast contract rejects
a native <select> styled as .app-input: 1px --border rule, 2px radius, 32px tall, 13px --font-sans
the visible <label> is bound by id; a control is never labeled by placement alone
fields holding machine values (keys, issuers, client ids, claim names, tenant keys) add .mono for --font-mono at 12px
header is plain surface (not gray) relying on a 1px --border bottom rule
selection wash uses --declare-soft plus a 3px --declare inset left marker, never lime — selection is positional as well as tinted
1px --border-soft row dividers, last row borderless
an irreducibly wide table scrolls rather than dropping columns; the scroller is role=region with an aria-label and tabindex=0 so a keyboard-only reader can focus and pan it

a row is interactive only when it carries a link: tbody tr:has(a) takes a --surface-hover wash and an inset --declare marker on focus-visible, and the linked cell underlines. A static readout row gets no hover, so the treatment never promises a click that is not there.
native <details>/<summary>: open state, keyboard operation and the expanded/collapsed announcement come from the platform
open is the initial state only — the element owns it afterwards
1px --border-soft divider between summary and body, matching the internal-divider rule
--code-bg block with --code-text in --font-mono (Fragment Mono), 2px radius, horizontally scrollable, dark in both modes
optional copy button via navigator.clipboard; copied feedback is a written word plus glyph, and may take the --evidence fill because it confirms capture
renders text, never markup: the code prop is escaped content, not HTML
